title: Rethinking Transfer Learning for Industrial Inspection: DINOv3 vs. ImageNet Pretraining Across RGB and X-ray Tasks
mechanism: Controlled comparison: DINOv3-distilled ConvNeXt is no better frozen but a much better initialisation under full long fine-tuning on RGB industrial segmentation; worse on greyscale X-ray.
evidence: R (full text): Severstal frozen 62.40 vs 62.04 mIoU; full fine-tune DINOv3 ConvNeXt-T +10.29 mIoU over ImageNet ConvNeXt-T, +10.59 over R50 (Mask2Former default schedule). GDXray: ImageNet 21.32 vs 7.88 AP50 frozen, 29.74 vs 27.84 fine-tuned.
adaptation: Redo A8 properly: DINOv3 ConvNeXt-S/B in smp U-Net++ with stride-2 stem, full fine-tune (not PF), 20k steps, vs ImageNet ConvNeXt of the same size. EL is greyscale like X-ray, so expect a null; it is cheap and closes the question.
min_experiment: DINOv3 ConvNeXt-B vs ImageNet ConvNeXt-B, 3 seeds + 5-fold CV; metric CV crack IoU / relF1@2, inactive IoU; kill if DINOv3 not above ImageNet by 0.01 crack IoU.
prior_overlap: A8 tested ConvNeXt-T under PF at 4k steps on F51 AP only; full fine-tune, 20k steps, larger ConvNeXt untested. Partly open.

alt_notes.adaptation: Benchmark design: include ConvNeXt-T ImageNet and ConvNeXt-T DINOv3 rows under the same fine-tune for 1-ch near-IR EL; prior that general FMs are not automatically better on EL.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Benchmark row pair only; no separate arm.

alt_notes.adaptation: Benchmark design: include ConvNeXt-T ImageNet and ConvNeXt-T DINOv3 rows under one fine-tune on 1-ch EL; prior that a general FM is not automatically better under greyscale modality shift.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Benchmark row pair only (already partly screened: DINOv3 ConvNeXt-T PF 4k steps, no sign); extend to full 20k schedule on folds.
